title: Bijou
subject: a rental viewing in Rathmines with forty other people where the agent calls a cupboard the second bedroom
caption: Irish post-punk in the current Dublin style. A melodic bass guitar picked high on the neck carrying the main riff; an angular clean guitar soaked in chorus playing clipped stabs, switching to blown-out fuzz in the choruses; tight motorik drums with a dry snare and loud floor toms; a droning organ note under the last chorus. Dry and close with little reverb, the bass and drums forward, the guitars lower in the mix. Male voice, a flat Dublin baritone in deadpan half-spoken Sprechgesang, chanting the chorus rather than belting it. 146 BPM, E minor. Sardonic, tight-jawed fury. No jangly indie-pop guitars, no big singalong chorus, no britpop swagger, no autotune, no synth pads, no American pop-punk.
lyrics:
[Intro - high melodic bass riff and dry drums]

[Verse 1]
Saturday viewing, Rathmines, half ten
Forty of us on the stairs, a queue out past the Spar
Agent in a gilet with a clipboard and a grin
Says have your references ready, it's very competitive

[Chorus]
Bijou, he says, bijou
The second bedroom is a press with a door
Bijou, he says, bijou
Two thousand one hundred a month

[Verse 2]
The shower's in the kitchen, he calls it open plan
There's a futon on the boiler, he calls it flexible
A lad behind me's offering six months up front
A girl is crying quietly in the hot press

[Chorus]
Bijou, he says, bijou
The second bedroom is a press with a door
Bijou, I say, bijou
And I hand him my references anyway

[Bridge - fuzz guitar and floor toms]
Bank statements, payslips, a letter from my mam
A letter from my mam to say I'm very tidy

[Outro - bass alone, then cut]
He'll be in touch
He won't be in touch

[Song ends abruptly]
